classification.difficultyReason: Recognise four quarter circles inside the square and subtract their total area.

content.prompt: A circle of radius $1$ is centred on each of the four vertices of a square of side length $2$. Find the area of the region enclosed by the four circles.

spec.description: A diamond-oriented square has a radius-1 circle centred at each vertex. Adjacent circles touch at the square's side midpoints; the central gap is bounded by four quarter-circle arcs. Decorative orange circle fill omitted.
spec.mathematics: Each square side has length 2. Circles have radius 1 and adjacent centres are distance 2 apart.
spec.answerVisibility: No solution labels, area values or extra construction lines.

answer.short:
$4-\pi$ square units.

Subtract four quarter circles from the square.
answer.worked:
Inside the square, each circle occupies a quarter circle of radius $1$.

$$\begin{align*}A&=2^2-4\left(\frac{\pi\cdot1^2}{4}\right)\\A&=4-\pi\text{ square units}.\end{align*}$$
